properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. It is dev_storyflow's wish #47 (session 62995724, 2026-09-27, while moving the project to the hosted graph), triaged 2026-09-28 from art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27. In their words: "Bulk 'is this already in the graph?' matcher for a list of texts, with per-item best hit and score." Their reason: migrating 71 memory files "meant grepping the exported JSON for file names and then searching by keyword per item. A bulk 'match these N texts against the graph, return best hit + score per item' would have made the population check one call (and made `rule:enumerate_the_population_before_acting_on_a_classification` cheap to obey)." That rule is storyflow's, not reflow2's.

WHY IT CAME UP: the issue beside it is root-caused in fact:root-cause-a-population-check-has-no-served-form-2026-09-28. search_design takes one query. relation_candidates takes an existing node. ingest_corpus_step is a write-extraction that dedupes by name within one type, and it is not offered on the hosted engine. create_nodes check_only validates the schema only. The one normalised matcher the server has, search_first (each text scored against its own self-score, with a floor at 0.5 of that), runs only as a guard after a write, at 7 single constructors.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE REPORTER'S: a read-only tool. It takes N texts and returns each one's best hit and a score. One call, no writes.
(b) EXPOSE search_first AS A READ. For each text, compute the near-match guard's comparison against the text's own score without writing it (for example, by scoring it in a throwaway index), and return the candidates with their ratio to that self-score instead of raw BM25. This is the only score the server has that can be compared across items, and it would agree by construction with what the write guard later says. Cost: new plumbing to get a self-score without a write. It also inherits the guard's own measured flaw, fact:the-near-match-guard-shows-three-of-a-nine-way-tie-so-relevance-is-decided-by-score-noise.
(c) A `queries: [...]` ARRAY ON search_design. N searches in one call, raw scores, plus each item's margin over its second hit. The cheapest option. Weakness, measured 2026-09-28: raw BM25 does not separate present from absent. A paraphrase of an existing rule ranked that rule 4th, at 20.9, while an item absent from the design got a best hit of 21.3.
(d) LET create_nodes check_only RUN THE NEAR-MATCH GUARD PER ITEM. The batch door already exists and already validates without writing, so "would these land as duplicates?" becomes one call on the path a migration is about to take anyway. Weakness: it answers for nodes already drafted, not for raw texts.
(e) DECLINE. Whether an item is represented is a judgement; the server's job is to hand back candidates, and search_design already does that one item at a time. Measured: the compute per call is negligible (0.69–0.79 s for a one-shot search, against 0.69–0.88 s for a no-op), so what batching saves is round trips and context, not server time.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a "score" per item invites a threshold, and no absolute threshold on BM25 means anything. The design's own measurement is that the same topic scored 4.48 and 35.75 under two phrasings (dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important). A lexical match also cannot see a paraphrase in someone's personal shorthand, which is what memory files are written in. So a false "not represented" would mint duplicates, and a false "represented" would silently drop an item. Whatever ships should return candidates with a normalised score and leave the verdict with the agent. What it can make cheap is the enumeration the storyflow rule demands, not the judgement.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 serve a bulk "is this already in the graph?" matcher (a list of texts in, the best hit and a score per item out), so that checking a population takes one call instead of grepping the export and searching item by item?
properties.rationale: Recorded open because the options differ in what the score MEANS (raw BM25 against a normalised self-score), and that decides whether any per-item verdict can be trusted. This is a separate question from whether to batch at all. Settling it is Anthony's call.
